record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on the standard symplectic torus, and more generally on an arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifold, does the quadratic lower bound for the growth of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits hold whenever the periodic orbit set is infinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Prove the conjecture for the tori

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectically aspherical symplectic manifold; that is, $\omega|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$ and $c_1(TM)|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$. A particular case of interest is the standard symplectic torus $(\mathbb{T}^{2n},\omega_0)$, where $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^n dx_i\wedge dy_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}/\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$.

Let $\varphi\colon M\to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian flow generated by a smooth function $H\colon S^1\times M\to\mathbb{R}$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k\in\mathbb{N}$ is a fixed point of $\varphi^k$; it is called primitive if $k$ is the minimal such integer. Two primitive periodic orbits are geometrically distinct if their underlying sets of points in $M$ are different. For $N\in\mathbb{N}$, denote by $P(\varphi,N)$ the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of $\varphi$ of period at most $N$.

Question: Suppose $\varphi$ has infinitely many geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits. Is it true that there exists a constant $c=c(\varphi)>0$ such that
$$P(\varphi,N)\ \ge\ c\,N^2$$
for all sufficiently large $N$? Resolve this in the case $M=\mathbb{T}^{2n}$ and, more generally, for arbitrary closed symplectically aspherical $(M,\omega)$.
artifact.status_search_result: For closed symplectically aspherical manifolds, the Conley conjecture (existence of infinitely many periodic orbits for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism) is established by Ginzburg and Hingston–Salamon–Hofer. Quantitative refinements give only generic results: for a $C^\infty$-generic Hamiltonian diffeomorphism the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of period $\le N$ grows at least like $N/\log N$. A universal quadratic lower bound for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with infinitely many periodic orbits, including on the standard torus $\mathbb{T}^{2n}$, does not appear to have been established and is reported as open in recent surveys on Hamiltonian dynamics.

status_evidence.title: The Conley Conjecture and Beyond
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses quantitative growth and notes that generic Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on aspherical manifolds have at least N/log N geometrically distinct periodic orbits of period ≤ N; stronger universal bounds remain conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Quadratic growth conjecture is discussed as an open refinement of the Conley conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Conley Conjecture Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of infinitely many periodic orbits in broader settings but does not give universal quadratic lower bounds on growth.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known; quantitative quadratic growth is not proved in general.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Fixed Points and Periodic Orbits of Hamiltonian Diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Ginzburg–Gurel results on forcing infinitely many orbits from a hyperbolic fixed point; quantitative growth rates remain limited.
status_evidence.claim: Ginzburg–Gurel results yield infinitely many orbits but not a universal quadratic bound.
